goal:
Extend this small library in two steps.
First: add `formatDuration(seconds)` in src/format.js, exported from src/index.js, which turns a non-negative integer number of seconds into the shortest of "<n>s", "<n>m" or "<n>h" that is exact (90 -> "90s", 900 -> "15m", 7200 -> "2h", 0 -> "0s"), and throws RangeError for a negative or non-integer number. With node:test tests.
Second, building on the first: add `roundTrip(text)` in src/round-trip.js, exported from src/index.js, which returns `formatDuration(parseDuration(text))`, with tests showing that "120s" becomes "2m" and "60m" becomes "1h".
`npm test` must pass after each step.
replanNote: Add one final milestone after the others: document formatDuration and roundTrip in README.md with one usage example each. Keep the existing milestones as they are.

memory.title: formatDuration contract
memory.content: formatDuration(seconds) in src/format.js is exported from src/index.js. It returns the largest exact unit: h if divisible by 3600, otherwise m if divisible by 60, otherwise s. 0 returns '0s'. Any non-integer or negative input throws RangeError. roundTrip can build on it.
memory.evidence: src/format.js and the src/index.js export line in the diff.

memory.title: roundTrip and error behaviour
memory.content: roundTrip(text) = formatDuration(parseDuration(text)). Text that is not an integer followed by s, m or h makes parseDuration throw TypeError. Negative or non-integer values throw RangeError from formatDuration. roundTrip is exported from src/index.js.
